problems.title: A sine value in the second quadrant
problems.question: $\sin\alpha=1/2$ and $\alpha\in[\pi/2,\pi]$. Find alpha.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The reference angle is π/6. In the specified quadrant, alpha is π−π/6=5π/6.

problems.title: A product of complementary sines
problems.question: Evaluate $2\sin15^\circ\sin75^\circ$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The expression is sin30°=1/2.

problems.title: Maximum of a reciprocal trigonometric function
problems.question: Maximize $2/(2+\sin x)$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The positive denominator is in [1,3]. The quotient is largest when the denominator is 1, attained at sin x=−1.

problems.title: A projection missing from the choices
problems.question: A point is distance a from a plane. An oblique segment makes 45° with the perpendicular to the plane. Find its projection length.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The perpendicular, projection and oblique segment form a right triangle. The opposite and adjacent legs at 45° are equal, so the projection is a.
problems.note: None of the printed choices a/√3, a√3/2, a/2, a/√2 equals the correct projection a for positive a.

problems.title: Distance between points above a plane
problems.question: A and B have distances 16 and 11 from a plane. Their perpendicular feet are distance 12 apart. Which listed AB is possible?
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: On the same side the height difference is 5, giving AB=13. On opposite sides it is 27, giving $AB=\sqrt{873}=3\sqrt{97}$.
Only 13 is listed.

problems.title: A squared tangent for an obtuse angle
problems.question: Find obtuse alpha with $\tan^2\alpha=1/3$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
formulas: Tangent is negative in quadrant II.
steps: Thus tan alpha=−1/√3 and the reference angle is 30°. The obtuse solution is 150°.

problems.title: Reduce a large angle
problems.question: Evaluate $\cos1320^\circ$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.

problems.title: A tangent from a cosine
problems.question: Alpha is acute and cos alpha=1/3. Find tan alpha.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The positive sine is $\sqrt{8/9}=2\sqrt2/3$. Divide by 1/3.

problems.title: Two perpendicular projections
problems.question: AO=2 is perpendicular to a plane. AB and AC make 60° and 45° with AO. Their projections OB,OC are perpendicular. Find BC.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The projections are 2√3 and 2. Therefore $BC=\sqrt{12+4}=4$.

problems.title: Equal distances from the sides of an equilateral triangle
problems.question: An equilateral triangle has side a. K is distance b from each side. Find its distance h from the triangle plane.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: For a projection inside the triangle, equal side distances place the projection at its centre. Its distance to a side is r.
Thus $h=\sqrt{b^2-a^2/12}$, requiring $b\ge a/\sqrt{12}$.
If the sides mean their entire supporting lines and exterior projections are allowed, an excenter has line-distance $a\sqrt3/2$. It gives the additional possible value $\sqrt{b^2-3a^2/4}$ when real.
problems.note: The usual intended projection is inside the triangle. With distances to supporting lines and no interior restriction, exterior excentres can give a second value.

problems.title: Closest intersections of a cosine and a horizontal line
problems.question: Find the smallest distance between distinct intersections of $y=\cos x$ and $y=\sqrt3/2$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: All points have the same y coordinate. Consecutive horizontal spacings alternate π/3 and 5π/3. The smaller is π/3.

problems.title: A sine identity true for every input
problems.question: Find the listed alpha for $\sin(x+\alpha)=\cos(x-\pi/4)$ for all real x.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The right side becomes sin(x+π/4). Hence alpha=π/4 modulo 2π; the listed value is π/4.

problems.title: Maximum on a restricted angular interval
problems.question: Where does $3\sin x$ attain its maximum on [115°,200°]?
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
formulas: Derivative with respect to a degree variable has the sign of cos x.
steps: Cosine is negative throughout the interval, so sine strictly decreases there. The largest value is at the left endpoint.

problems.title: A point equidistant from four square vertices
problems.question: A square has side 19. A point is distance x from all four vertices. Which listed x is impossible?
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The projection is the square centre, so x≥19/√2=9.5√2. The listed 9√2 is below this bound.
The other listed distances, 10√2,19,199, exceed the bound and can be realized by suitable h.

problems.title: Complementary inclination angles
problems.question: An oblique segment makes alpha with a plane. Its sine is half the sine of the angle it makes with the plane normal. Find cos alpha.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: Thus tan alpha=1/2. From $1+\tan^2\alpha=1/\cos^2\alpha$, the positive cosine is 2/√5.

problems.title: Symmetry of the cosine graph
problems.question: Which listed axis or point is a symmetry of $y=\cos x$?
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: This is the condition for reflection symmetry in the y axis. The other listed symmetries fail, for example by testing (0,1).

problems.title: A homogeneous trigonometric quotient
problems.question: Evaluate $(3\sin x-\cos x)/(3\cos x-\sin x)$ if tan x=2.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
formulas: Divide numerator and denominator by cos x, nonzero when tangent is defined.

problems.title: Recover a sine-cosine product
problems.question: $\sin x+\cos x=k$. Find $\sin x\cos x$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: Rearrange k²=1+2sin x cos x.

problems.title: Distance across a dihedral angle
problems.question: On faces of a 120° dihedral angle, AC=2,BD=3 are perpendicular to the edge and CD=1 lies on the edge. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The perpendicular-to-edge components contribute $4+9-12(-1/2)=19$. The along-edge component contributes 1.
Hence AB=√20=2√5.

problems.title: A parallelogram admitting equal distances to its sides
problems.question: A point outside a parallelogram’s plane is equidistant from all four sides. What type must the parallelogram be?
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
formulas: Squared spatial side distance = squared height + squared planar side distance.
steps: Its projection is equidistant from both pairs of parallel side lines, hence is their common midline intersection, the parallelogram centre.
Equal distances to all four sides mean the two altitudes are equal. With area $S=ah_a=bh_b$, equal altitudes force adjacent sides a=b.
Therefore the parallelogram is a rhombus; a square is possible but not necessary.

problems.title: Period after taking absolute value
problems.question: Find the least positive period of $|\cos7x|$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
formulas: $|\cos t|$ has least positive period π.
steps: The inside angle grows by π when x grows by π/7. This is the smallest repeat.

problems.title: Square roots of squares
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt{(1+2\cos60^\circ)^2}-\sqrt{(1-2\sin60^\circ)^2}$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The first term is |2|=2. The second is |1−√3|=√3−1. Subtraction gives 3−√3.

problems.title: Locate a principal inverse-cosine value
problems.question: Which interval contains $\arccos(-\pi/8)$?
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
formulas: Arccos takes values in [0,π] and is greater than π/2 for a negative argument.
steps: $-1<-\pi/8<0$, so its arccosine lies strictly between π/2 and π.

problems.title: Distance to a line from above a right triangle
problems.question: Right triangle ABC has CA=15,CB=20. CD=5 is perpendicular to its plane. Find distance from D to AB.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The hypotenuse is 25, so CH=300/25=12. Then DH=√(25+144)=13.

problems.title: Perpendicular to two lines in a plane
problems.question: DC is perpendicular to CA and CB, with D outside triangle ABC’s plane and M on AB. Find angle DCM.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
formulas: A line perpendicular to two intersecting lines of a plane is perpendicular to that plane.
steps: Thus DC is perpendicular to every line through C in the plane, including CM.

problems.title: Sum the cosine-equation roots in an interval
problems.question: Find the sum of solutions to $\cos(\pi x/6)=1/2$ in [0,20].
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: The roots in the interval are 2,10,14. Their sum is 26.

problems.title: Height above a regular hexagon
problems.question: A is distance √52 from every regular-hexagon vertex and √43 from every side. Find its height h above the plane.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: Subtract to get $R^2/4=9$, so R²=36. Then h²=52−36=16.

problems.title: Two oblique lengths with ratio one to two
problems.question: Two oblique segments from one point to a plane have lengths in ratio 1:2 and projections 1 and 7. Find the lengths.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: $4(h^2+1)=h^2+49$ gives h²=15. Therefore the lengths are √16=4 and √64=8.

problems.title: A trigonometric equation using squares
problems.question: Solve $\cos^2x+5\sin^2x=2$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: $1+4\sin^2x=2$ gives sin²x=1/4. Thus sin x=±1/2.
All solutions are $x=k\pi\pm\pi/6$, with integer k.

problems.title: Rectangle area from a spatial equidistant point
problems.question: M is distance 13 from every rectangle vertex and distance 12 from its plane. The rectangle perimeter is 28. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: R=5 and d=10, so a²+b²=100. The perimeter gives a+b=14.
Then 196=100+2ab, hence area ab=48.

problems.title: Cosine of a sum in the second quadrant
problems.question: $\sin\alpha=2/3$ and alpha lies in [90°,180°]. Find cos(alpha+60°).
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: Cos alpha=−√5/3. Therefore the requested cosine is $-\sqrt5/6-(2/3)(\sqrt3/2)=-(\sqrt5+2\sqrt3)/6$.

problems.title: Interpolate signed distances along a segment
problems.question: AB does not cross a plane. C divides AB with AC:CB=3:2. Distances of A,C from the plane are 6 and 10. Find B’s distance.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
formulas: On one side of a plane, distance varies linearly; $h_C=(2h_A+3h_B)/5$.
steps: $50=12+3h_B$, hence $h_B=38/3$. It is positive, consistent with no crossing.

problems.title: All sine-equation roots in a degree interval
problems.question: Find all solutions of sin6x=1/2 in (0°,180°).
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: Dividing by 6 gives $x=5^\circ+60^\circ k$ or $25^\circ+60^\circ k$. In the interval, k=0,1,2 for each family.
Thus the six values are 5°,25°,65°,85°,125°,145°.

problems.title: A line parallel to a plane
problems.question: AB=12 is parallel to a plane. AC and BD go to the plane, perpendicular to AB on opposite sides. Their plane inclinations are 45° and alpha, with tan alpha=2/3; CD=13. Find the line-plane distance h.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
steps: Because the projections lie on opposite sides of AB, their transverse separation is $5h/2$. Their along-AB separation is 12.

problems.title: A parameter producing exactly seven roots
problems.question: $\cos\sqrt{2ax-x^2}=1$ has exactly seven real solutions, a>0. Find a and their sum.
problems.idea: Use the relevant triangle or trigonometric identity, with domains and alternative configurations checked.
formulas: $2ax-x^2=a^2-(x-a)^2$; the square root ranges over [0,a]; cos t=1 iff t=2πk.
steps: Each level $2\pi k<a$ gives two symmetric roots $x=a\pm\sqrt{a^2-4\pi^2k^2}$. A level equal to a gives just the middle root x=a.
To obtain an odd count of seven, the top level must be a. With a=2πm, there are 2m+1 roots, hence m=3 and a=6π.
The roots are three pairs symmetric about a and the middle root a. Their sum is 7a=42π.
